html:
SMTO-CFG-0088 — SMTO can't turn on that Skill for this Task

GUID: c814f5b1-c956-5d75-bf40-882db5661709
Slug: capability-activation-not-grantable
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • The Agent wanted a Skill that can't be turned on in this Task, because of how the Task was started or because something the Skill needs isn't available. Nothing was turned on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Skill was installed or switched on after this Task began, use a new request for that work; a running Task keeps the Skill list it started with. SMTO only adds Skills that were on the Task's list when it started.
  2. If the Agent mode menu by the message box says Ask, switch it to Agent. Ask mode doesn't run Skills that change things, so they can't be turned on there.
  3. Open Capabilities, find the Skill, and check it isn't marked Unavailable and that none of its tools are set to Never or − Exclude. SMTO can't turn on a Skill when tools it depends on are blocked or still need setup.
  4. Check which steps the old Task already finished before you send the new request. This avoids repeating work that already happened.

What success looks like

  • In the new Task, a Capabilities activated for this request note appears and the work continues.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO; a Workflow or Gateway limit may be blocking this Skill. Allowing it again won't help, because your permission alone can't lift that limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activation classified the Skill as not grantable: it is absent from the accepted manifest, cannot be compiled into a permitted prospective ceiling under the hard tool limits, lacks grant provenance or a conversation grant service, or its required tools or dependencies are outside the ceiling.

What this means

  • Activation cannot compile a permitted prospective capability under hard restrictions, lacks required grant provenance/service, or cannot provide the Skill's required tools/dependencies. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Activation cannot compile a permitted prospective capability under hard restrictions, lacks required grant provenance/service, or cannot provide the Skill's required tools/dependencies.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect accepted hard-tool limits, Skill dependencies and grant provenance; a user yes alone cannot remove upstream restrictions.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's capability_ceiling (manifest, skill_tools, skill_dependencies, grant_provenance.hard_tool_ids and agent_mode) against the Skill's uses_tools (classify and prospective in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_activation.py; answer_in in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_grants.py). Fix the upstream restriction, tool exclusion or missing dependency for a new run, or continue with permitted alternatives.
  • This capability cannot be enabled within the accepted environment and authority constraints.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported eligible configuration supplies the capability and required dependencies, or permitted alternatives are used.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
